core_obligations: Prove (1): the double dual of M is torsion free by the preceding lemma, and a submodule of a torsion free module is torsion free, so a reflexive M is torsion free (proof lines 5178-5179).

Assume M is finite, choose generators x_1 to x_n whose first r images form a basis of M tensor K, write the remaining generators in that basis with coefficients k_ij in K and clear denominators with c in R (proof lines 5180-5187).

Build the maps alpha : R^r to M and beta : M to R^r whose two composites are multiplication by c and put them into the square involving j, concluding that kernel and cokernel of j are annihilated by c, which is assertion (2) (proof lines 5188-5213).

Prove (3): if M is torsion free then beta is injective, hence j is injective, and conversely injectivity of j gives torsion freeness because the double dual is torsion free already (proof lines 5214-5217).

The nearest public record is 337 (5577-5633, tag 0AVB, reflexive modules and codimension-one intersections), which is the main theorem of the same section on reflexive modules and starts about 360 lines later; this card counts the short preliminary lemma of that section, not the intersection theorem.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the basic comparison between reflexivity and torsion freeness over a domain (statement lines 5165-5174): a reflexive module is torsion free, and for a finite module M the natural map j to the double dual has torsion kernel and cokernel and is injective if and only if M is torsion free. The proof is a 42-line argument (proof lines 5177-5218) in which the interesting half is the finite case: the author chooses a partial system of generators whose images form a basis of M tensor K, writes the remaining generators in that basis over the fraction field, clears denominators with one element c to obtain two maps alpha and beta between R^r and M whose composites are multiplication by c, and then draws a commutative diagram with four occurrences of j to conclude that the kernel and cokernel of j are annihilated by c. The final step for (3) reads injectivity of j off the injectivity of beta. No step is left to the reader and the only cited input is the preceding lemma of the same section.
